title: ISO/IEC 27001 — Information Security Management
shortDescription: Confidentiality, integrity, availability — the three-word core of the standard behind 'ISO certified' data security claims.
genZNote: Your data's three basic rights: nobody unauthorized sees it, nobody quietly changes it, and it's actually there when you need it.

sections.heading: What It Is
bullets: Full reference: ISO/IEC 27001 — jointly published by ISO and IEC, since information security spans both organizational and technical/electrotechnical territory.
Specifies requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS) — a systematic approach to managing sensitive information so it stays secure.
Part of the broader ISO/IEC 27000 family, which includes related standards like ISO/IEC 27002 (a detailed code of practice for security controls, used alongside 27001).

sections.heading: The Core Objective — the 'CIA Triad'
bullets: Confidentiality — ensuring information is accessible only to those authorised to access it.
Integrity — safeguarding the accuracy and completeness of information and processing methods (i.e. no unauthorized or accidental alteration).
Availability — ensuring authorised users have access to information and associated assets when they actually need it.

sections.heading: Risk-Based Approach and Controls
sections.body: Like the other modern management-system standards, ISO/IEC 27001 is built around identifying information-security RISKS relevant to the organization's specific context, then selecting and implementing appropriate CONTROLS to treat those risks — it does not mandate one fixed universal security setup for every organization. The standard's Annex A lists a reference set of controls (spanning organizational, people, physical, and technological categories) that organizations select from based on their own risk assessment — not every control applies to every organization.

sections.heading: Organizational Context and Continual Improvement
bullets: Requires the organization to understand its own internal/external context and the needs/expectations of interested parties (customers, regulators, employees) before designing its ISMS.
Follows the same continual-improvement, High Level Structure pattern as ISO 9001/14001/45001 — an ISMS is never a one-time setup.
Certifiable — organizations can be independently certified as ISO/IEC 27001 compliant, which is increasingly required in cloud-services, fintech, and data-processing contracts.

sections.heading: Why This Shows Up Outside IT Departments
sections.body: ISO/IEC 27001 certification has become a common vendor-assessment requirement well beyond traditional 'IT companies' — hospitals, laboratories, and research institutions handling sensitive patient or research data increasingly need it too, since data security has become part of overall organizational trustworthiness, not a separate concern bolted onto a lab's core quality system.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: ISO/IEC 27001 is the certifiable Information Security Management System standard, built around protecting the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of information through a risk-based approach.
keyFacts: Jointly published by ISO and IEC — hence 'ISO/IEC 27001', not just 'ISO 27001' in strict citation.
Core objective: the CIA triad — Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability.
Annex A provides a reference set of security controls, selected based on the organization's own risk assessment — not a one-size-fits-all checklist.
commonConfusion: ISO/IEC 27001 (the certifiable requirements standard) and ISO/IEC 27002 (a detailed code of practice for controls, used alongside it) are related but distinct documents.

highYieldFacts: The CIA triad — Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability — is the core objective of ISO/IEC 27001.
ISO/IEC 27001 is jointly issued by ISO and IEC, unlike single-body standards such as ISO 9001.
commonTraps: Do not write it as simply 'ISO 27001' in a precise-citation context — the correct designation is 'ISO/IEC 27001' since IEC co-publishes it.
Do not confuse 'Availability' (authorised access when needed) with 'Integrity' (accuracy/no unauthorized change) — both are frequently swapped in distractor options.
mustRemember: Annex A controls are SELECTED based on risk assessment — not every organization applies every control.
ISO/IEC 27001 follows the same High Level Structure as ISO 9001/14001/45001, enabling integrated management systems.
possibleQuestions: What do the three letters in the 'CIA triad' (as used in ISO/IEC 27001) stand for?
Why is the standard designated 'ISO/IEC 27001' rather than just 'ISO 27001'?
